candidate_findings.title: Sliding-window rollups lack a deterministic watermark and transaction contract
candidate_findings.claim: The analytics scanner may use either a time window or a checkpoint and may persist either a sequence or timestamp checkpoint. The generic projector atomicity rule does not explicitly say that all analytics rollup keys and the analytics checkpoint commit as one transaction. The span also does not define authoritative event time, evaluation time, inclusive boundaries, late-event handling, clock rollback, expiry when no new events arrive, or concurrent-scan arbitration.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A sliding 5h/24h/7d result can retain expired events, omit late records, or advance its checkpoint past partially written keys. Two periodic/on-demand scans can also overwrite one another with results computed from different watermarks, producing plausible but incorrect usage and error dashboards.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define a single scan watermark model, event-time source and boundary rules, late-event policy, full-window expiry behavior, scanner lease or compare-and-swap rule, and an atomic rollup-set-plus-checkpoint commit. Add deterministic fixtures for no-new-event expiry, late arrivals, clock skew, crash between writes, and overlapping scans.

candidate_findings.title: Missing background worktree fields fail open into main-project context
candidate_findings.claim: A background run enqueued from a bound thread may omit its worktree path and branch, and consumers are instructed to interpret absence as main-project context. There is no required check against the frozen thread binding, no explicit context-kind discriminator, and no rejection or quarantine rule for a bound-thread event missing its worktree snapshot.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A legacy producer, serialization bug, partial event, or replay mismatch can redirect mutation-capable background work from an isolated worktree into the main project without an explicit authority decision.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Freeze and persist `execution_context_kind`, `worktree_id`, path, branch, and HEAD at enqueue time; require them for bound-thread work; validate them against the binding snapshot; and fail closed on omission or mismatch. Define an explicit legacy migration path that cannot mutate main-project state silently.

candidate_findings.title: Single-field TODO mutation events cannot safely encode structural revisions
candidate_findings.claim: `todowrite` may create and reorder items, and post-execution corrections must create a new revision, yet the minimal mutation event addresses one todo and one field with unconstrained old/new values. It lacks plan_revision_id, base revision, transaction or batch ID, ordering generation, tombstone/create semantics, dependency validation, expected prior value, and a stable actor identity beyond agent/user.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A multi-item reorder or revision can become partially visible after a crash, concurrent edits can interleave, and replay cannot distinguish a complete structural revision from several unrelated field changes. Duplicate delivery can corrupt order or dependencies.

candidate_findings.title: Sensitive activity and web payloads lack an end-to-end data-lifecycle contract
candidate_findings.claim: The span persists terminal commands, structured operation inputs, and full web bodies/source sets. It links cache storage to a TTL table, but does not define how TTL, deletion, legal hold, export, immutable attempt snapshots, and history references interact. It also omits payload classification, secret redaction, encryption, project/account access control, ref integrity, garbage collection, and size or rate quotas.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Commands and web inputs can contain credentials, private URLs, user content, or regulated data. Inline history can outlive an expired cache blob, deletion can leave orphaned sensitive bodies, forged refs can cross scopes, and unbounded crawl/research payloads can exhaust storage.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define sensitivity classes and redaction before persistence, encryption and ACL boundaries, immutable-ref hashing and scope binding, TTL/deletion/legal-hold propagation, export sanitization, blob reachability and garbage collection, maximum sizes/counts, and security and quota test fixtures.

candidate_findings.title: Unsaved-editor implementation fields cannot prove recovery of buffer content
candidate_findings.claim: The rules require local buffer state, capture metadata, host/path identity, and write availability, but the implementation key contains only project and path hash, and its enumerated stored fields contain cursor/scroll/selection, an undo reference, and an unsaved flag. It does not require the actual buffer bytes or content ref, base-file hash/version, host identity, capture generation/time, destination identity, write availability, checksum, or durable ordering. The conflict rule therefore has no specified persisted baseline against which to decide that the file changed.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: After a crash, PM may know that a buffer was dirty while being unable to reconstruct the edits or identify the correct remote destination. Path reuse, rename, case normalization, hash collision, or remote host ambiguity can restore edits into the wrong file, and conflict detection can compare against an unspecified baseline.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Persist encrypted buffer content or an integrity-bound content ref, base content hash/version and save generation, host and destination identity, canonical path rules and collision handling, capture sequence/time, write availability, lifecycle and retention rules, and atomic snapshot ordering. Define recovery tests for crash timing, rename, deletion, remote unavailability, path collision, and concurrent views.

candidate_findings.title: Projection freshness can remain misleadingly current and has no defined health relationship
candidate_findings.claim: The requirements distinguish freshness from health and later require LSP disclosure of current, refreshing, stale, degraded, or unavailable. The implementation defines only the three freshness values and defines current merely as just resolved. It does not define health values, transition triggers, resolved_at or observed_at, TTL, restart semantics, dependency invalidation, precedence between stale and degraded/unavailable, or which actor may mark a projection current.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A projection restored after a restart or network loss can remain labeled current indefinitely, while another consumer labels the same state degraded or unavailable. GUI history and recovery surfaces can then overstate operational readiness or write availability.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define separate versioned freshness and health state machines, timestamps/watermarks, invalidation inputs, restart defaults, authority and precedence, write-availability linkage, and UI rendering rules. Add transition tests for disconnect, stale cache, refresh failure, degraded recovery, and user retry.
